answer: Each agent claims a grove plot, splits one soil core, and seals half in a jade-tagged jar keyed to that agent alone. An auditor blind-retests the sealed half, recomputing its yarrow mass against its declaration; mismatch over five percent, plot reuse, or jar reuse burns the bond. The agent locks 70 credits and pays 25+5(k-1) for the kth core; the 1,000th pays 5,020. One thousand fakes lock 70,000 and pay 2,522,500. A rented-core ring fails: one sealed half cannot match two declarations, and the ledger rejects a second claim. An honest agent pays 25 once and recovers its bond after passing.
